newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alcoa Australia says to extend gold mine's life.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa Australia says to extend gold mine's life.

text.p: Alcoa of Australia Ltd said on Thursday it had extended the life of its Hedges gold mine in Western Australia for a further two years after exploration work turned up more gold.
The mine, located adjacent to the Boddington lode 120 km south east of Perth, was expected to close in late 1997.
"We've extended the life until late 1999 and we continuing to do further exploration in the area," an Alcoa spokesman said.
The mine produced 109,000 ounces of gold in 1996, he said.
Alcoa of Australia is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 39.25 percent by WMC Ltd.
The remaining interest is held by QBE Insurance Group Ltd .
